0fb1572a: What is the most abundant chemical element in the universe?
Hydrogen makes up about 75% of the universe's ordinary (baryonic) matter. It is the fuel of stars through nuclear fusion.
8360c0ae: What is the largest ocean in the world?
The Pacific Ocean covers 165 million km², more than all the land on Earth combined.
62824273: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
Au (from the Latin aurum) is the chemical symbol for gold, a precious metal with atomic number 79.
317097a7: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa between 1503 and 1519. The world's most famous painting hangs in the Louvre.
a8e8573c: What is the capital of Australia?
Canberra is Australia's federal capital, a planned city often mistaken for Sydney.
eb73ee70: How many bones does the adult human body have?
The adult human body has 206 bones. A baby is born with around 270 to 300 bones, some of which fuse during growth.
b6f405ce: What was the most populous country in the world in 2024?
India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, with more than 1.42 billion people.
f5aba9cb: Mars is the “red planet” because of the iron oxide covering its surface. It is the fourth planet from the Sun.
df7bf5ba: Which composer was deaf when he wrote his Ninth Symphony?
Ludwig van Beethoven composed his Ninth Symphony (1824) while almost completely deaf.
86f6330a: What is the longest river in the world?
The Nile (about 6,650 km) is generally considered the longest, although the Amazon is sometimes measured as longer.
de4e9d9d: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
The speed of light is 299,792 km/s, the universal constant c, fundamental to Einstein's relativity.
7488afc9: Which French author wrote Les Misérables?
Victor Hugo published Les Misérables in 1862. It is one of the most widely read novels in the world.
0e32579d: Who developed the theory of general relativity?
Albert Einstein published general relativity in 1915, revolutionizing our understanding of gravity.
1dfeca56: What is the highest mountain in the world?
Mount Everest rises to 8,848.86 m in the Himalayas. It was first climbed in 1953.
f979d779: How many permanent teeth does an adult normally have?
An adult normally has 32 permanent teeth, including 4 wisdom teeth. Without them, there are 28.
2c5715bb: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
Canada has the longest coastline, about 202,000 km including its islands.
59c52bfc: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
Mandarin has the most native speakers, about 900 million.
18208f30: Who wrote Hamlet, Romeo and Juliet and King Lear?
William Shakespeare (1564-1616) is the greatest playwright in English literature, with some 37 plays and 154 sonnets.
3e828b96: What is the largest desert in the world?
Antarctica is the largest desert, with 14.2 million km², a cold desert. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.
0e3be65f: George Orwell published 1984 in 1949, a prophetic dystopia about totalitarianism and surveillance. “Big Brother is watching you.”
d17e2ae6: What is the chemical formula of water?
H2O is the chemical formula of water: two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.
bbb99ed0: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups?
Brazil is the most successful, with 5 World Cups (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002).
0f504c02: How many planets are there in the solar system (since 2006)?
There have been 8 planets since 2006, when Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
baff2a37: Antonio Vivaldi composed The Four Seasons around 1720, one of the most played and recognizable classical works.
2e577187: How many chromosomes does a human normally have?
A human normally has 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs, including one pair of sex chromosomes (XX or XY).
c3d34a9b: What is the official motto of France?
“Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité” (Liberty, Equality, Fraternity) is France's national motto, born of the 1789 Revolution.
7ca0b65c: Michelangelo sculpted the David, a Renaissance marble masterpiece 5.17 meters tall.
fed27e65: What is the capital of Japan?
Tokyo is the capital of Japan and the largest metropolitan area in the world, with about 37 million people.
6b4fd539: What is the largest country in the world by area?
Russia is the largest country, with 17.1 million km², spanning 11 time zones.
5ecd65f6: What is the largest organ of the human body?
The skin is the largest organ: it covers 1.5 to 2 m² and weighs 3 to 5 kg.
8f88338a: Which country is called the “Land of the Rising Sun”?
Japan is the “Land of the Rising Sun”: Nihon means “origin of the sun”.
9dd91730: What is the fastest land animal?
The cheetah can reach around 112 km/h over short distances and accelerate to 100 km/h in about 3 seconds.
1cac94d6: Alexander Graham Bell filed his telephone patent on February 14, 1876, just hours before his rival Elisha Gray.
51019a7e: Who is the author of One Hundred Years of Solitude?
Gabriel García Márquez published One Hundred Years of Solitude in 1967, a masterpiece of magical realism. He won the Nobel Prize in 1982.
2e78a800: What is the chemical formula of table salt?
NaCl (sodium chloride) is the formula of table salt, an ionic compound essential to life.
c5f3d7db: What is the largest continent in the world?
Asia is the largest continent, with 44.6 million km², and home to about 60% of the world's population.
c66a3fb7: Which Dutch painter created The Starry Night in 1889?
Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in June 1889 at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence.
fb95a494: Which lake holds the largest volume of fresh water in the world (about 22% of the world's surface fresh water)?
Lake Baikal (Siberia, Russia) is the deepest lake in the world (1,642 m) and holds about 22% of the world's surface fresh water. Lake Superior is larger in area but much shallower.
6a2a85d6: Who is the author of The Stranger and The Plague?
Albert Camus published The Stranger (1942) and The Plague (1947). He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1957.
eb9153f2: How long does the Earth take to orbit the Sun?
The Earth takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun (more precisely 365.2422 days), hence the leap year every 4 years.
14f45ab0: Who composed the Star Wars score?
John Williams composed Star Wars (1977), one of the most recognizable film scores in history.
efecae8d: What is the heaviest animal in the world?
The blue whale can weigh up to about 190 tonnes; its heart alone weighs around 180 kg.
af3866a8: What is the smallest sovereign country in the world?
Vatican City is the smallest country, at 0.44 km² with about 800 residents, the seat of the Catholic Church.
ef4f3573: Which musician is called the “King of Rock and Roll”?
Elvis Presley (1935-1977) is the “King of Rock and Roll”. His first recordings in 1954-1955 helped launch rock as a mass phenomenon.
100903f6: What is the square root of 144?
The square root of 144 is 12, because 12 × 12 = 144.
a16a694b: What is the process by which plants make their food?
Photosynthesis turns sunlight, water and CO2 into sugars and oxygen, the foundation of the food chain.
173e0472: Who is the author of The Divine Comedy?
Dante Alighieri wrote The Divine Comedy (about 1308-1320), a founding work of the modern Italian literary language.
240679fc: Roughly how many countries are there in the world (UN)?
There are 193 UN member states, plus 2 observer states (the Holy See and Palestine).
1d2f0672: What is π (pi) rounded to 5 decimal places?
π ≈ 3.14159 is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, an irrational and transcendental number.
89e30d7c: Miguel de Cervantes published Don Quixote in 1605 and 1615. It is often considered the greatest novel ever written.
0f3d3269: Which planet has the most known moons?
Saturn holds the record: as of 2025, it has more than 270 known moons, far ahead of Jupiter.
153f30e3: Which scientist stated the law of universal gravitation?
Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal gravitation (1687), F = Gm₁m₂/r², in his Principia Mathematica.
16d1c933: What is the average Earth-Sun distance (1 astronomical unit)?
The Earth-Sun distance is about 150 million km, known as the astronomical unit (AU).
a6f77160: What is the lightest metal among those solid at room temperature?
Lithium is the lightest solid metal, so light that it floats on water.
c783e6cf: Which painter is known for the Water Lilies series?
Claude Monet painted the Water Lilies in his garden at Giverny, a series of about 250 oil paintings of his pond.
7829ed5d: What is the theory of the origin of the universe 13.8 billion years ago called?
The Big Bang is the standard cosmological model: the universe began in an extremely hot, dense state and has been expanding ever since.
c248ed08: Who wrote the tragedy Oedipus Rex in ancient Greece?
Sophocles wrote Oedipus Rex around 429 BC. Aristotle held it up as the model tragedy in his Poetics.
7057b0e1: Who is the author of the Discourse on Method (1637)?
René Descartes published the Discourse on Method in 1637: “I think, therefore I am” (Cogito, ergo sum).
5da42a1f: What was the approximate world population in 2024?
The world population reached 8 billion in November 2022 and is projected to reach 9 billion around 2037.
b1b8a7ee: What is the most expensive painting ever sold at auction (2017)?
Salvator Mundi, attributed to Leonardo da Vinci, sold for 450.3 million dollars at Christie's in 2017.
427bad26: What is the second most abundant element in the universe?
Helium is the second most abundant element after hydrogen, making up about 24% of ordinary matter by mass.
48b451de: Who founded Apple Computer with Steve Jobs in 1976?
Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs (and briefly Ronald Wayne) founded Apple in 1976. Wozniak designed the first computers.
8aa22180: What is the name of the elementary particle linked to how other particles get their mass?
The Higgs boson is the particle associated with the Higgs field, which gives other particles their mass. It was discovered at CERN in 2012.
c2c9cec4: The yen (¥) has been Japan's currency since 1871, one of the most traded currencies in the world along with the dollar and the euro.
cf025676: How many faces does a regular dodecahedron have?
A regular dodecahedron has 12 pentagonal faces. It is one of the 5 Platonic solids.
ada7cdd0: Which Russian author wrote War and Peace?
Leo Tolstoy published War and Peace between 1865 and 1869, a sweeping novel considered one of the greatest ever written.
2275c2ff: What is the longest bone in the human body?
The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, about a quarter of a person's height.
7123e6cc: What is the speed of sound in air at 20°C?
The speed of sound in air at 20°C is about 343 m/s (1,235 km/h). It varies with temperature and the medium.
a762c92f: Diego Velázquez painted Las Meninas (The Ladies-in-Waiting) in 1656, a masterpiece of the Spanish Baroque, now in the Prado Museum.
d9ca432f: What is the smallest continent in the world?
Australia is the smallest continent, with about 7.7 million km².
66368f78: Which scientist formulated the laws of planetary motion?
Johannes Kepler formulated his three laws of planetary motion (1609-1619): planets orbit in ellipses, not perfect circles.
118e9120: The pancreas produces insulin in the islets of Langerhans. This hormone regulates blood sugar by letting cells absorb glucose.
cb49f507: Which Shakespeare play is based on the legend of the Danish prince Amleth?
Hamlet is based on the Danish legend of Amleth, a prince who feigns madness to avenge his murdered father.
6d03e184: What is Einstein's formula for energy?
E = mc² is Einstein's famous equation: energy (E) equals mass (m) times the speed of light squared (c²).
6ba6305d: Who is the author of The Master and Margarita?
Mikhail Bulgakov wrote The Master and Margarita (published posthumously in 1966-1967), a satirical fantasy novel considered one of the great books of the 20th century.
4719832d: Which language is the most spoken in the world (all speakers combined)?
English is the most widely spoken language in the world, with about 1.5 billion speakers (native and learners). Mandarin has the most native speakers.
9e6b53ae: Which country was the world's largest oil producer in 2024?
The United States has been the world's largest oil producer since 2018, thanks to the shale oil boom in states such as Texas and North Dakota.
de603f53: Which gas do plants absorb for photosynthesis?
Plants capture carbon dioxide and the Sun's energy to make sugars, releasing oxygen.
35f59ebb: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system and the closest to the Sun.
10dde267: What is the largest planet in the solar system?
Jupiter, a gas giant, is so big that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.
ca73b553: What is the hottest planet in the solar system?
Although farther from the Sun than Mercury, Venus is the hottest: its thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat, above 450°C.
6dac3739: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
The symbol Fe comes from the Latin ferrum. F is the symbol for fluorine.
3a73ae39: Which chemical element has the symbol Na?
Na comes from the Latin natrium. Nitrogen's symbol is N, neon's Ne and nickel's Ni.
7e31cf2a: Which gas makes up about 78% of the air we breathe?
Dry air contains about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and a little under 1% argon.
904d8806: Which scientist proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859, after his observations during the voyage of the Beagle.
1afa9fa4: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903, then in Chemistry in 1911. She is the only person honored in two different sciences.
435e5fd0: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100°C (212°F). At altitude, it boils at a lower temperature.
059916cd: How many hearts does an octopus have?
An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood through the gills and one through the rest of the body. Its blood is blue.
4a931bef: What is the only mammal capable of true flight?
Bats flap their wings to fly. Flying squirrels and colugos can only glide.
b7071360: Which blood type is known as the “universal donor” for red blood cells?
O negative red blood cells can be given to almost anyone. AB positive people are universal recipients.
fdca804c: Roughly how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
Light covers the 150 million kilometers between us and the Sun in about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.
6e9b29e0: Who developed the first rabies vaccine, in 1885?
In 1885, Louis Pasteur successfully vaccinated young Joseph Meister, who had been bitten by a rabid dog.
43604762: Which French physicist discovered radioactivity in 1896?
Henri Becquerel discovered that uranium emits radiation. He shared the 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie.
378b0e04: The ohm is named after the German physicist Georg Ohm. The volt measures voltage, the ampere current and the watt power.
db35f418: How many chambers does the human heart have?
The heart has two atria and two ventricles.
40fee63d: What is the largest land animal?
The African elephant can weigh more than 6 tonnes. The giraffe is the tallest, but not the heaviest.
ccf14d97: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature. It was once used in thermometers.
e1b09f7a: What is the pH of pure water at 25°C?
Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7. Below that, a solution is acidic; above, it is basic.
4aaad92b: Which vitamin does the skin produce when exposed to sunlight?
Ultraviolet rays allow the skin to produce vitamin D, essential for strong bones.
f0fb9eb9: Which Greek scholar is said to have shouted “Eureka!” in his bath?
According to legend, Archimedes discovered in his bath the principle of buoyancy that bears his name.
e1508b82: How many sides does a hexagon have?
A hexagon has six sides. A pentagon has five, a heptagon seven and an octagon eight.
a773cb8f: What do the angles of a triangle add up to?
In a triangle, the three angles always add up to 180°.
96135992: What do you call a number divisible only by 1 and itself?
2, 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13 are prime numbers: they have exactly two divisors.
3f74152f: What is the smallest prime number?
1 is not prime because it has only one divisor. 2 is the smallest prime number, and the only even one.
3287a587: Which Greek mathematician gave his name to the theorem about right triangles?
According to the Pythagorean theorem, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
95785197: What value does the Roman numeral L represent?
In Roman numerals, L is 50, C is 100, D is 500 and M is 1,000.
d01525b8: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, aviator and writer, published The Little Prince in 1943. It is one of the most translated books in the world.
244b370b: Who wrote the poetry collection The Flowers of Evil?
Charles Baudelaire published Les Fleurs du mal in 1857. The collection was condemned for “offending public morals”.
a6d32e4b: Who is the author of Madame Bovary?
Gustave Flaubert published Madame Bovary in 1857. He was prosecuted, then acquitted.
3345db62: Which Émile Zola novel tells the story of a miners' strike in northern France?
Germinal (1885) follows Étienne Lantier, who leads a strike at a mine in northern France.
07961761: Which playwright wrote The Imaginary Invalid?
The Imaginary Invalid is Molière's last play. He collapsed during the fourth performance, in 1673, and died a few hours later.
604f4a8e: Alexandre Dumas published The Three Musketeers in 1844. D'Artagnan joins Athos, Porthos and Aramis.
9cba8444: Who wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas?
Jules Verne introduced Captain Nemo and his submarine, the Nautilus, in 1869-1870.
8f42be75: Who is the author of the Harry Potter series?
J. K. Rowling published the first book, Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, in 1997.
d496afc7: Jane Austen published Pride and Prejudice in 1813. Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy are its protagonists.
cb73dbe8: Which Greek poet is traditionally considered the author of the Odyssey?
The Iliad and the Odyssey are attributed to Homer. The Odyssey tells of Odysseus's long journey home to Ithaca.
2c2d8ed7: Which author created the detective Sherlock Holmes?
Sir Arthur Conan Doyle introduced Sherlock Holmes in 1887 in A Study in Scarlet.
8ea21a26: Which novelist created the detective Hercule Poirot?
Hercule Poirot, the Belgian detective, first appeared in 1920 in The Mysterious Affair at Styles.
f7c84fba: Who wrote the fable The Crow and the Fox?
Jean de La Fontaine published his Fables from 1668 on. The Crow and the Fox is one of the most famous. The story itself goes back to Aesop.
221a0ab5: Which poet wrote “Le Dormeur du val” (The Sleeper in the Valley)?
Arthur Rimbaud wrote this sonnet in 1870, at sixteen, during the Franco-Prussian War.
429f60a8: Who wrote The Lord of the Rings?
J. R. R. Tolkien, an Oxford professor, published The Lord of the Rings in 1954-1955.
31cf53b9: Who wrote The Red and the Black?
Stendhal published The Red and the Black in 1830. Julien Sorel, a carpenter's son, dreams of rising in society.
d5a7bada: Which writer is the author of In Search of Lost Time?
Marcel Proust's seven-volume novel contains the famous madeleine episode. The second volume won the Prix Goncourt in 1919.
907271ab: Who wrote the philosophical tale Candide?
Voltaire published Candide in 1759, mocking blind optimism: “we must cultivate our garden”.
0bbb2188: Picasso painted Guernica in 1937 after the bombing of the Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.
ec9e503d: Which Norwegian painter created The Scream?
Edvard Munch made several versions of The Scream, the first in 1893.
c3d32cff: Which artist painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, in the Vatican, between 1508 and 1512, including the famous Creation of Adam.
c9e31c37: In which museum is the Mona Lisa displayed?
Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa is displayed at the Louvre in Paris. It was stolen in 1911 and recovered in 1913.
7c9ae47e: Which surrealist painter is famous for his melting clocks?
The melting clocks appear in Salvador Dalí's The Persistence of Memory (1931).
8256c8f5: Which movement takes its name from a Monet painting, Impression, Sunrise?
A critic mocked Monet's painting by calling its artists “Impressionists”. The name stuck.
f6cfd9ca: Auguste Rodin's The Thinker was originally intended for his Gates of Hell.
bf3f6dc2: Which Dutch painter created Girl with a Pearl Earring?
Johannes Vermeer painted this portrait around 1665. It is held at the Mauritshuis in The Hague.
b50f64cc: Which pop artist is famous for his portraits of Marilyn Monroe?
Andy Warhol reproduced Marilyn Monroe's face in silkscreen prints with bright colors, starting in 1962.
617b996f: Which architect designed the Louvre Pyramid?
The Chinese-American architect I. M. Pei designed the glass pyramid, inaugurated in 1989.
d3fc0808: Which Austrian composer wrote the opera The Magic Flute?
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart composed The Magic Flute in 1791, the year he died, at 35.
dc4f9697: How many strings does a classical guitar have?
A classical guitar has six strings. An electric bass usually has four.
3db50699: Which French composer wrote the Boléro?
Maurice Ravel composed the Boléro in 1928. The same theme is repeated in one long, continuous crescendo.
606b5404: Which Polish composer is famous for his piano nocturnes?
Frédéric Chopin, born in Poland in 1810, wrote almost exclusively for the piano. He lived in Paris.
9c935b32: How many keys does a standard piano have?
A standard piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.
b3dc7e2b: Which Greek philosopher was Plato's teacher?
Socrates wrote nothing. His thought is known to us through the dialogues of his student Plato.
ea1888f1: Which German philosopher wrote Thus Spoke Zarathustra?
Friedrich Nietzsche published this work between 1883 and 1885. In it he develops the idea of the Übermensch.
68b264c8: Which Enlightenment philosopher wrote The Social Contract?
Jean-Jacques Rousseau published The Social Contract in 1762, defending the sovereignty of the people.
035ae607: Which Chinese thinker's teachings are collected in the Analects?
The Analects gather the sayings of Confucius, recorded by his disciples. Laozi is associated with Taoism.
f8f96b84: How many squares are on a chessboard?
A chessboard has 8 rows of 8 squares, 64 squares alternating light and dark.
f62869d8: How many colors does the rainbow traditionally have?
Seven colors are traditionally named: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
841cdfe9: What is the official language of Brazil?
A former Portuguese colony, Brazil has Portuguese as its official language. It is the largest Portuguese-speaking country in the world.
a052e586: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
The Taj Mahal, in Agra, was built in the 17th century by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife.
92af8d26: The barometer measures air pressure. The anemometer measures wind and the hygrometer humidity.
d50a8c4e: How many days are in a leap year?
A leap year has a February 29, for a total of 366 days. It generally comes around every four years.
d5846e63: How many stars are on the flag of the European Union?
The 12 gold stars symbolize unity and perfection. Their number does not depend on the number of member countries.
bed3a7b9: Which holiday is celebrated on May 1 in France?
May 1 is Labor Day (la fête du Travail), a public holiday. People traditionally give each other lily of the valley.
